Executive Summary for Chemical, Manufacturing, and Oil Refining Facilities
Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policies
Corteva (Owner) and The Dow Chemical Company (Operator) remain firmly committed to the safety of employees, the public, and the environment. This commitment is demonstrated through a comprehensive accidental release prevention program, which encompasses process design, installation, operating procedures, maintenance, and employee training. Our policy is to implement effective controls to prevent the release of regulated substances.
Stationary Source and Regulated Substances
The Corteva-owned facility contains one RMP-regulated substance above the threshold quantity: sulfur dioxide.
Worst-Case and Alternative Release Scenarios
Administrative controls and mitigation measures are in place to limit the impact distances for each reported scenario, where permitted and applicable. EPA RMP*Comp and MARPLOT were used to evaluate both worst-case and alternative scenarios.
General Accidental Release Prevention Program and Chemical-Specific Prevention Steps
Our facility complies with the accidental release prevention requirements of 40 CFR part 68. The following sections summarize the key elements of our release prevention program:
	Process Safety Information: We maintain detailed records describing chemical hazards, operating parameters, and equipment design for all processes.
	Process Hazard Analysis: Comprehensive studies are conducted to identify and control process hazards efficiently. We use methodologies such as What If, Checklist, and LOPA. Recommendations from hazard analyses are addressed promptly.
	Operating Procedures: Written procedures cover all modes of operation, including startup, normal and temporary operations, emergency shutdown, emergency operations, and shutdown after turnarounds. These procedures are regularly reviewed and accessible to all relevant personnel.
	Training: A robust training program ensures that employe

es are competent in operating procedures. Refresher training is provided at set intervals and as needed.
	Mechanical Integrity: Regular maintenance checks are performed on process equipmentincluding pressure vessels, storage tanks, piping, relief and vent systems, emergency shutdown systems, controls, and pumpsby qualified personnel. Any deficiencies are corrected safely and promptly.
	Management of Change: Written procedures govern changes in process chemicals, technology, equipment, and procedures. Affected employees are informed and trained on modifications.
	Pre-Startup Reviews: Safety reviews are conducted for new and modified processes to confirm readiness for safe startup.
	Compliance Audits: Regular audits (no more than every three years) ensure compliance with RMP requirements. Corrective actions are implemented as needed.
	Incident Investigation: All incidents that result in, or could reasonably result in, a catastrophic release are investigated to identify causes and corrective actions. Reports are retained for at least five years.
	Employee Participation: Employees are encouraged to participate in process safety management and accident prevention. Employees are involved in creation of scenarios and implementation of protection layers.  They have access to all RMP-related information, including process hazard analyses.
	Contractors: Contractors are evaluated for safety performance before selection. They are informed of potential hazards and emergency procedures relevant to their work.
Five-Year Accident History
No accidents meeting RMP reportable criteria have occurred at the Corteva facility in the past five years.
Emergency Response Plan
The facility maintains a written emergency response plan addressing accidental releases of hazardous materials. The plan covers first aid, medical treatment, evacuations, notifications to local agencies and the public, and post-incident decontamination. Emergency equipment is regularly inspected and maintained,

and the plan is updated as needed. Coordination with the Brazoria County Community Awareness Emergency Response (CAER) network manage by Brazoria County Petrochemical Council Local Emergency ensures alignment with local emergency planning.
As the plant operator, The Dow Chemical Company leads immediate response efforts and coordinates with the community and external services. Corteva partners with Dow to communicate facility changes that may affect emergency planning.
Dow Emergency Services and Security (ES&S) provides integrated site services for the protection of people and assets, including emergency response, site security, and maintenance of emergency equipment.
Planned Changes to Improve Safety
Continuous improvements are made based on findings from our prevention program. Recent initiatives include installing automatic shut-off of HVAC system to shelter in place building, removing large amounts of asbestos from a building on site, installing higher integrity safety system on critical pieces of equipment, and introducing a process clearing chemical to eliminate residual chemicals during maintenance line breaks.
